subject: Purchase-path assessment: reserved vs flexible & hosting tier selection
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Jul 2026 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Purchase-path assessment: reserved vs flexible & hosting tier selection

Hi Laura,

Thanks again for the demo today — appreciate you walking us through the integration goals and expected throughput for Q4. As discussed on the call, we want to make sure procurement has a clean path that aligns with Octane's purchasing rules (PO cadence, vendor onboarding, payment method). Below is a short recap and the recommended next steps from Redwood's side so your procurement and finance teams can evaluate quickly.

Recap (brief):
- Estimated steady-state: ~600k tokens/day with spikes to ~1.2M for product launches.
- Data residency: US-only for customer-facing API calls.
- Security: SOC 2 and customer-managed KMS required for the private deployment option.

Options we discussed (high level):
1) Hosted (Redwood API) — fastest time to value, card or PO via marketplace (standard terms). Good for proof-of-concept and short-term on-demand.
2) Dedicated (reserved capacity) — predictable throughput with committed monthly GPU pools. Supports PO-based billing and reserved pricing (recommended for production traffic).
3) Private (VPC/on-prem) — for regulated workflows; requires an enterprise agreement and longer procurement lead time.

Procurement considerations we heard from you: preference for PO, prefer vendor onboarding via marketplace only if it shortens the approval timeline.

Recommended commercial alignment (our suggested path):
- Short term: Start on Hosted to hit product milestones (card or marketplace PO if marketplace short-circuits procurement).
- Production: Plan for Dedicated with a 6–12 month reserved commit tied to a PO (pricing tiers below) — reduces per-token cost and meets PO billing requirements.
- If procurement demands isolated infrastructure or KMS control, prepare a Private deployment SOW; this adds procurement lead time but gives full control.

Attachments: redwood-pricing-matrix.xlsx (summary of hosted vs dedicated price bands), procurement-checklist.pdf (paperwork we typically need for PO onboarding).

Next steps / asks:
1) Can you confirm who on your procurement team will own vendor onboarding and whether marketplace enrollment is an option?
2) Do you have a timing target for issuing a PO for a pilot (if so, rough dates)?
3) Are there any non-standard contract terms (data retention, IP, or indemnity) your legal team will push back on?

If it's useful, I can put together a one-page commercial recommendation (hosted pilot + dedicated conversion timeline) and get Ben on a quick sync to map internal approval owners.

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Thanks — I'm Ben on Commercial Pricing. Quick confirmation from our side:

- Pilot: Hosted (card or marketplace PO) works fine; we'll quote a pilot band with an upgrade path credit if you convert to Dedicated within 90 days.
- Production: Recommended Dedicated reserved pool (we typically see 20–35% unit-cost reduction vs hosted at your volume). We can support PO billing for dedicated contracts; standard net-30 terms (or marketplace billing if that expedites onboarding).
- Private: We'll need to engage Solutions/Engineering early (2–3 week prep) and expect a longer procurement cycle; include SOW for KMS integration.

Action items from Redwood: we will send a one-page recommendation (pilot -> dedicated timeline) and an example 6-month committed quote by Friday EOD. I'll include the line-item for conversion credit and a short note on expected migration effort.
